messages:
Lena: Quick check-in from today’s allocator follow-up. We still need a compact way for the runtime to express short-lived pins/spill-intent and a safe compaction orchestration that doesn't surprise KV caches.

Omar: Proposal: introduce a "soft-reserve" lease object returned by allocator.request_soft_reserve(id, ttl_ms, priority). It acts like a hint but is revocable. Lease = {lease_id, version, expires_at}. Runtime either releases or the allocator revokes/expires.

Vik: Important: make the lease revocation explicit and observable so user-space subsystems can react. Suggest callbacks or a pollable lease-status API so decoders/KV layers see revokes before dereferencing freed memory.

Carlos: For compaction, we should avoid in-place destructive moves. Handshake idea: 1) runtime asks for compaction plan, 2) allocator responds with plan + peak_memory_estimate + recommended_quiesce_ms, 3) runtime quiesces (stop KV writes), 4) allocator allocates new contiguous backing and populates, 5) allocator publishes remap table, 6) runtime swaps pointers and acknowledges, 7) allocator frees old backing.

Lena: That mirrors our safety goals. Two concerns: peak memory headroom during copy, and long-tail latency if quiesce windows are long. We should support incremental micro-compaction too (small copies + repeated remaps) to reduce headroom.

Omar: Micro-compaction needs careful remap sequencing. Each micro-step must be atomic: allocator provides a micro-remap blob that only updates a subset of pointers. Runtime applies incrementally. If an apply fails, we stop and roll back later.

Vik: Rollback triggers are messy. Better to require positive ack before allocator frees anything. If a micro-step ack fails, allocator keeps old mapping and retries later. No in-place free until ack. Simpler and safer.

Carlos: We also need a cost-aware admission API: allocator.compaction_capacity() -> bytes_available_for_compaction, and allocator.estimate_compaction_cost(region_id) -> bytes_needed. If bytes_needed > bytes_available, allocator returns a suggested ETA. Scheduler can pick low-util nodes or defer.

Lena: Runtime feature-flag plan: start with leases behaving like hard-pins (compat mode) on older agents, then flip to soft-reserve in a staged rollout. Add a node-level flag to enable micro-compaction. Canary path: dedicated pool -> 2% hosted -> 25% region -> wide.

Omar: Telemetry to add ASAP: soft_lease_count, lease_revoke_rate, avg_lease_ttl_ms, live_fragmentation_pct, compaction_peak_headroom_pct, compaction_attempts, compaction_success_rate. Use these to auto-toggle the soft-reserve feature if fragmentation increases too much.

Vik: Safety invariants for the doc: (a) allocator never frees old physical pages without explicit runtime ack; (b) remap tables are versioned and atomic; (c) revocation must be eventually visible to all pointer-holders; (d) compaction must be schedulable with an estimate and budget. I'll draft these into the design doc.

Carlos: I'll prototype the compaction_budget and estimate endpoints on the allocator API. Will include micro-compaction stubs (no-op copy routines) for the first pass so we can exercise telemetry.

Lena: I'll add runtime integration: request_soft_reserve, poll_lease_status, accept_remap, apply_remap-ack. Also e2e harness that runs encoders + batching to measure steady-state fragmentation across 12h.

ops-bot: Created issue https://git.company/infra/5077 for soft-reserve leases + compaction orchestration. Runbook template attached.

Lena: Great. Ping me once PRs exist and paste them into the ticket. We'll review in the next arch sync. :white_check_mark:
